newsitem.title: USA: U.S., two Koreas start new round of talks.
newsitem.headline: U.S., two Koreas start new round of talks.

text.p: Diplomats from the United States, South Korea and North Korea began a new round of talks on Monday toward negotiating a formal end to the 1950-53 Korean War, a U.S. State Department official said.
The official said senior envoys from the three countries appeared to be in a relaxed mood, shaking hands and exchanging pleasantries before the one-day meeting started in a New York hotel.

The U.S. official quoted the North Korean delegation leader, Vice Foreign Minister Kim Gye Gwan, as saying: "Last time we were concerned that there might be a premature baby, but this time we're not concerned about a premature baby."
The delegations of senior officials first met in March in New York to discuss a proposal by Washington and Seoul for four-nation peace talks that would eventually also involve China.
The proposed four-party negotiations would aim to replace the armistice of 1953 with a formal peace treaty.
Communist North Korea, threatened by famine, agreed in principle in April to join the peace talks but linked its participation to food aid and an end to U.S. trade sanctions.
The armistice that ended the fighting on the Korean peninsula did not technically end the 1950-53 war.

In New York on Monday, North Korean and South Korean delegation leaders told each other they hoped for good results from their meeting, a follow-up to talks in March and April to discuss a proposal by Washington and Seoul for the four-nation peace talks.

According to a U.S. official, the North Korean delegation leader, Vice Foreign Minister Kim Gye Gwan, said: "Last time we were concerned that there might be a premature baby, but this time we're not concerned about a premature baby."
